title: Three-year multicenter surveillance of community-acquired Listeria monocytogenes meningitis in adults

claims.text: In a multicenter series of community-acquired bacterial meningitis, the leading organisms were S. pneumoniae (48.5%), N. meningitidis (22.6%), and L. monocytogenes (16.5%).
claims.byte_quote: Streptococcus pneumoniae (135, 48.5%), Neisseria meningitidis (63, 22.6%), Listeria monocytogenes (46, 16.5%)

claims.text: L. monocytogenes is the third most frequent cause of community-acquired bacterial meningitis, after S. pneumoniae and N. meningitidis.
claims.byte_quote: _Lm_ is the third most frequent cause of community-acquired bacterial meningitis, after _Streptococcus pneumoniae_ and _Neisseria meningitidis_

claims.text: L. monocytogenes meningitis accounted for 16.5% (46/278) of acute community-acquired cases in adults in this series.
claims.byte_quote: The incidence of acute community-acquired _Lm_ meningitis in adults was 16.5% (46/278)

claims.text: Estimated incidence of L. monocytogenes meningitis is 0.2 cases per 100,000 adults per year in developed countries.
claims.byte_quote: The estimated incidence is 0.2 cases per 100.000 adults per year in developed countries

claims.text: L. monocytogenes meningitis occurs mainly in immunocompromised patients, newborns, and elderly individuals, though previously healthy adults can also be affected.
claims.byte_quote: This entity occurs mainly in immunocompromised patients, newborns, and elderly individuals, although previously healthy adults can be affected as well.

claims.text: Older age was independently associated with Listeria meningitis (OR 1.026).
Immunosuppression was independently associated with L. monocytogenes meningitis (OR 2.520).
Sixty-eight percent of Listeria meningitis patients were immunocompromised.
Among immunocompromised Listeria patients, 41% were receiving immunosuppressive therapy and 27.5% had haematological or solid malignancy.
claims.byte_quote: Twelve (41%) patients were receiving immunosuppressive therapy, 8 (27.5%) had haematological and solid malignancy

claims.text: An elevated CSF/blood glucose ratio was independently associated with L. monocytogenes meningitis (OR 39.42).
L. monocytogenes appears as Gram-positive rods on Gram stain.
CSF Gram stain is negative in two-thirds of L. monocytogenes meningitis cases and may be misleading in many of the rest.
claims.byte_quote: the Gram stain is negative in two-thirds of the cases of _Lm_ meningitis, and may be misleading in many of the remaining cases
